evidence.snippet: Melian reviews its own pull requests in rounds. After each fix pass, a Melian round runs: from the `melian round` workflow, which runs the default branch's build, or from the branch's own build on a host. A pull request that changes Melian's review code needs a round from its own build, since the default branch's build cannot exercise it; [the Actions rounds decision](decisions/2026-11-06-actions-rounds-run-default-branch-code.md) says why the workflow runs the default branch's. The workflow posts its comment and sets `melian/review` as the machine user `melian-status-bot`, whose token only the default branch's round can read, so a builder reads that login's comment and no other as the round's; [the decision](decisions/2026-11-08-round-comment-as-the-machine-user.md) says why. The run records the comment's body as a `melian/round-comment` status, which no one can edit, so a comment a writer edited after it posted fails the check, and so does one holding another comment's body; [the decision](decisions/2026-11-14-round-records-its-comment-body.md) says why. Codex's adversarial review and a review of record run beside the rounds. The loop ends when a round finds nothing above advisory apart from policy notices. `AGENTS.md` says who runs each part.
